title: The labour movement and socialism
summary: As industry grew, trade unions organized to protect workers and improve wages and conditions. In 1864 a mass meeting of European trade unionists in London founded the First International, whose rules said the working classes must win their own emancipation. Socialists then built organized parties in many countries, and in Germany a mass working-class movement. On 14 July 1889 over 1,000 delegates founded the Second International in Paris. Its belief that workers' solidarity would prevent war was dashed by the First World War.

The 19th-century international socialist movement provided the theoretical and organizational lineage for 20th-century communist movements.
